heroLead: Grindstone was built as a coal-patch town, and like most patch communities in Fayette County, its mineral title history runs a lot deeper than the houses on the surface suggest.
intro: Grindstone sits near California, PA, in a part of Fayette County shaped almost entirely by coal mining in the early 20th century. Company-built patch towns like this one often had coal, oil, and gas rights severed from the surface separately, sometimes years apart, and Grindstone is no exception.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Grindstone, whether the interest traces back to an old coal-era severance, a more recent Marcellus lease, or a fractional share split among family members.

sections.heading: A patch town's layered mineral history
paragraphs: Coal company deeds around Grindstone frequently reserved or conveyed oil and gas rights on different terms than the surface or coal itself, which means today's owners sometimes hold an interest that looks unusual on paper until you trace it back to its origin.

sections.heading: Marcellus activity in this stretch of the county
paragraphs: Development near Grindstone has followed the broader pattern for this part of Fayette County — present, but less dense than the wet-gas core counties to the west, with value depending heavily on the specific tract.

sections.heading: Our process for a property like this
paragraphs: We pull the recorded chain of title, confirm what era's severance actually governs the oil and gas interest, and review any lease or royalty documents before naming a figure.
Fayette County's Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown holds the records that ultimately confirm what you own.

faqs.question: Grindstone was a coal-patch town — how does that affect my oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Coal, oil, and gas were often severed separately in patch-town deeds, sometimes at different times. We trace the recorded history to confirm which document governs the oil and gas interest you actually own.

faqs.question: Is my Grindstone-area interest worth anything if there's no well on it yet?
faqs.answer: Possibly — leased but undrilled acreage still has value depending on lease terms and nearby activity, so it's worth reviewing rather than assuming it isn't.

faqs.question: Where are Grindstone-area deeds recorded?
faqs.answer: Through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown, the same office that covers the entire county.

faqs.question: How do I confirm whether my Grindstone interest is still under an active coal-era severance?
faqs.answer: We trace the recorded chain of title back through the original severance instrument and any subsequent transfers, which tells us definitively whether the interest you hold today still traces to that coal-era document.
